item.title: What If the Problem Is Too Much Capital?
item.description: It needs to go somewhere, from imperial adventures to AI.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Amazon Earnings: Jassy Has a Trillion-Dollar AWS in His Sights
item.description: Similar to investor reaction to Alphabet Inc.’s earnings a day earlier, the stellar performance of Amazon.com Inc.’s cloud unit was overshadowed by jitters around other parts of the business when the company reported third-quarter results on Thursday. A softer-than-expected forecast for Christmas and a miss on quarterly revenue prompted a sharp selloff after hours. At one point shares were down 7% after dropping 4.25% earlier in the day.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: AI's Coming Dystopia Was Skewered 300 Years Ago by Jonathan Swift
item.description: It takes a rare genius to write a satire that is still read 300 years after its publication. Most satire dwells on the peccadilloes of soon-to-be forgotten politicians. And it takes a unique genius to write a satire that is more relevant today than it was in the days of powdered wigs and knee breeches. That is exactly what Jonathan Swift achieved when he published Gulliver’s Travels Into Remote Regions of the World on Oct. 28, 1726.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Halloween Candy Tamed The Holiday Maybe a Little Too Well
item.description: It’s that time of year when toddlers, tweens and even some teens will go door to door, sacks outstretched for candy. While they’ll mumble “trick or treat,” tricks are few and far between these days.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Mihm

item.title: AI Labs’ Cybersecurity Gains Come at the Economy’s Expense
item.description: Last week programmers raced to fix flaws that have been known for years in a programming language that is itself more than three decades old. Why the rush? Because the language, called PHP, is used by about a billion websites worldwide, and the defects would allow an attacker to take over a web server. OpenAI, whose models helped discover the vulnerabilities, called them “one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.”
item.dc:creator: Gautam Mukunda

item.title: Musk Is on to Something With His Stock Handout Idea
item.description: When Elon Musk pledged to give a share of SpaceX to each child in the US, the proclamation was met with a certain amount of skepticism. Regardless of Musk’s motivation or whether his promise comes to fruition, he has — inadvertently or not — hit on a worthwhile idea: Giving both future and current workers a stake in American business is a good way to lift their fortunes, reduce inequality and bolster support for free-market capitalism.
item.dc:creator: Nir Kaissar

item.title: Republican Senate Spending in Texas and Kansas Signals Midterms Anxiety
item.description: Anxious Republicans are free to self-medicate with daydreams of a massive public polling error. But GOP groups wouldn’t be spending big money in red states galore to defend the party’s Senate majority if their own internal survey data wasn’t flashing blue.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: Trump’s Venezuela Strategy Needs More Than Oil Deals
item.description: The stunning comeback that secured Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a fourth term a president of Brazil has given the politics of Latin America a major twist. The colossus of South America will remain on a leftist track, countering the remarkable rightward shift across the region.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: Midterm Voters Pine for the Days When Democrats Led the Economy
item.description: A half century of history is converging with public opinion polls showing US voters prefer Democrats as stewards of the economy for the first time in more than a decade. It took less than 24 months for 58% of Americans to say they're worse off under President Donald Trump than under Joe Biden, correcting the prevailing media narrative that declared the 46th president a failure after Trump was elected a second time without a majority in 2024. The Biden economy turns out to be superior to any prec
item.dc:creator: Matthew A. Winkler

item.title: Serbian Election: Student List Needs Its Own Hungary's Peter Magyar
item.description: Serbia’s Alexander Vucic, who lost power in the country’s recent elections, is not its first authoritarian leader to be undone by a student uprising. The Otpor! (Resistance!) movement that toppled Slobodan Milosevic more than a quarter century ago was the prototype for the popular revolts that have since swept across the former Communist bloc. If today’s Serbian students hope to turn power into change, there are lessons to be learned from that history.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: In Replacing Lagarde, the ECB Should Reject Radical Change
item.description: Kevin Warsh’s five-month-old tenure as head of the Federal Reserve offers an instructive counterexample for the European Central Bank as it seeks to replace President Christine Lagarde, who announced that she will step down on Feb. 7.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Anthropic $100 Billion IPO Bet Is the Only Market That Matters Now
item.description: The mood music is sounding a little more mellifluous for Anthropic PBC’s mega initial public offering. On the same day it was launched this week, Meta Platforms Inc. announced a bravura $95 billion share sale, and tech stocks have crawled above their October low.
item.dc:creator: Chris Hughes

item.title: Energy Shock: Cost-of-Living Crises Don’t Need to Cost So Much
item.description: Time and again, cost-of-living crises like the current global energy-price shock confront governments with a dilemma: Either do the difficult work of identifying and supporting the vulnerable, or throw money at everyone whether they need it or not. Time and again, they overwhelmingly choose the latter.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Made in China: Are Chinese Brands Nearing a ‘Made in Japan’ Moment?
item.description: In 1970, my uncle came back from Japan with a battery-operated Godzilla. Eleven-year-old me — a kaiju cinema fan for years by then — loved it. But a couple of weeks later, the monster stopped wobbling around on its thick metal legs. I sadly reached for an explanation that today would be called a meme: What did you expect, it was made in Japan.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: Weil Gotshal Collapse: Is This Big Law’s Lehman Moment?
item.description: Weil’s collapse has us wondering whether lawyers are the new bankers.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: China Shock Is Harder to Fight for Thailand With the Superpower Next Door
item.description: After a lean few years, Thailand’s economy is showing signs of improvement. Deflation has given way to inflation of almost 3%, while policymakers are upgrading growth forecasts. With the recovery still modest, however, officials have little reason to rush: Absent a major upheaval, they can take their time lifting interest rates from historically low levels.It's an encouraging picture — but one that tells only part of the story.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Grand Theft Auto May Be Outdated in the AI Video Game Age
item.description: Video games need AI not just to fix the industry’s economics, but to usher in a new era of creativity.
item.dc:creator: Gearoid Reidy

item.title: Run on the Law Firm
item.description: Weil Gotshal, bankers turned lawyers, onion protests, more sports bets.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: South Korea’s Military Ambitions Get a Reality Check
item.description: The deck is stacked against a significant shift in military control on the Korean Peninsula, yet that is exactly what South Korean President Lee Jae Myung is staking his leadership on. It’s the right idea, at the wrong time.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Pollard

item.title: Machado Must Embrace Patience to Secure Venezuela’s Political Future
item.description: María Corina Machado’s return to Venezuela has some of the same sweep and drama of Simón Bolivar’s return more than two centuries ago. But if she wants her story to end better than one of the great heroic deeds of 19th-century Latin America, she will have to match her passion for her nation with patience for change.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Spinetto
